This is a test of the refactor.inline.variable code action on Gon initializers
whose identifiers are not lexical references: named-argument labels, and the
contextual variants of the predeclared Result, which has no package.

-- go.mod --
module example.com/a
go 1.27

-- a/a.go --
package a

func scale(width, height int) int { return width * height }

func _() int {
	v := scale(height: 2, width: 3)
	return v //@codeaction("v", "refactor.inline.variable", result=inlineNamed)
}

func _(err error) Result[int, error] {
	var res Result[int, error] = .Err(err)
	return res //@codeaction("res", "refactor.inline.variable", result=inlineVariant)
}

-- @inlineNamed/a/a.go --
package a

func scale(width, height int) int { return width * height }

func _() int {
	v := scale(height: 2, width: 3)
	return scale(height: 2, width: 3) //@codeaction("v", "refactor.inline.variable", result=inlineNamed)
}

func _(err error) Result[int, error] {
	var res Result[int, error] = .Err(err)
	return res //@codeaction("res", "refactor.inline.variable", result=inlineVariant)
}

-- @inlineVariant/a/a.go --
package a

func scale(width, height int) int { return width * height }

func _() int {
	v := scale(height: 2, width: 3)
	return v //@codeaction("v", "refactor.inline.variable", result=inlineNamed)
}

func _(err error) Result[int, error] {
	var res Result[int, error] = .Err(err)
	return .Err(err) //@codeaction("res", "refactor.inline.variable", result=inlineVariant)
}
